structured_output.analysis: The best measured recipe, iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e), is about 0.0005 bits per weight under the 403/128 budget. That leaves no room for a plain upgrade, so any extra bits have to come from somewhere else. Last round's proposals were refused only because their rationale quoted a rounded KL value that matched no record, so this round quotes only exact ledger numbers. At equal bits the per-layer methods are already the best choice for the layers that hold the most loss: for example, 27.up has gptq_int3 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded) against rht_gptq_int3 0.00774363 (E8972491007e7). That leaves two ways forward. One is option changes that cost no bits (act_order, damp). The other is to free bits by using group_size=256 on the 109 rht_gptq_int3 layers, which cuts the per-group scale overhead from about 0.148 to about 0.074 bits per weight. Those bits then pay for 4-bit upgrades on the MLP layers where the loss is concentrated.

proposals.name: act_order_all
proposals.rationale: No layer changes, so the bit count is the same as iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e). This turns on act_order=true for every GPTQ-family method. Most of the loss sits in 3-bit MLP layers, for example 27.up gptq_int3 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded) and 3.up rht_gptq_int3 0.0064177 (E6f4f7ea296d5), where act_order usually lowers GPTQ error.

proposals.name: g256_rht3_4up
proposals.rationale: Setting group_size=256 on the rht_gptq_int3 layers frees scale bits, which pay for four upgrades. 27.up: gptq_int3 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded) to gptq_int4 0.00216589 (Efea8c18d2abc). 14.down: rht_gptq_int2 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065) to rht_gptq_int3 0.00181478 (E90bd4b2f3645). 27.gate: rht_gptq_int3 0.00498703 (Efa0bb391da67) to rht_gptq_int4 0.00153131 (Ef428ac081334). 3.up: rht_gptq_int3 0.0064177 (E6f4f7ea296d5) to gptq_int4 0.00237732 (Ef4ee8cb4969e).

proposals.name: g256_rht3_4up_actorder
proposals.rationale: Same upgrades as g256_rht3_4up, with act_order=true added to offset the coarser group_size=256. Upgrade numbers: 27.up gptq_int4 0.00216589 (Efea8c18d2abc) vs gptq_int3 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded); 14.down rht_gptq_int3 0.00181478 (E90bd4b2f3645) vs rht_gptq_int2 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065).

proposals.name: damp_low_all
proposals.rationale: No layer changes, so the bit count is the same as iso_3.15 (E514ab09c524e). This sets damp=0.005 on every GPTQ method to apply the Hessian correction more fully. The main targets are the 2-bit layers such as 14.down rht_gptq_int2 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065).
